title: review (other model, opus): C-O4 fix round 1 on serve.py from security review T-0152 (T-0153, executed by claude:sonnet)
spec: Review ONLY the T-0153 delta: `git diff be42500 38db9bb` in worktree wt/T-0153 (orchestrator/serve.py, tests/test_serve.py, .orchestrator/repos.toml.example). Fix round for security review T-0152; confirm each item resolved: (1) auth compare encodes both sides (utf-8 surrogateescape) and any exception yields 401, tested with a non-ASCII header; (2) MAX_BODY_BYTES 65536 → 413 and MAX_GOAL_CHARS 20000 → 400 with tests; (3) import-failure message names the mcp package and uv sync, no dependency group, pyproject untouched; (4) module docstring and repos.toml.example state requester scoping is kgpt's job; (5) the lock test proves the flock is actually held (not just that the file exists), plus tests for the multi-repo GET fan-out, the not-configured 404 and invalid JSON → 400. Also check nothing regressed from T-0147 (auth on every route but /healthz, 409 via list_goals, per-slug lock spanning clone+check+start, clone stderr never in a body). Run `uv run python -m unittest tests.test_serve -q` once. Verdict approve or request_changes with file:line comments; keep to real defects.
acceptance: Verdict approve or request_changes with file:line comments
Each of the five T-0152 items confirmed resolved or named unresolved with evidence
No regression of the T-0147 guarantees

comments.issue: Unredacted subprocess stderr reaches the response body, contradicting the T-0147 guarantee this module states at line 22 ("clone stderr is never safe to echo verbatim, and it must never reach a response body at all"). The clone path is careful (generic "clone failed" + CREDENTIAL_RE on the log line), but goals.start refusal reasons are passed through raw: goals.py builds them as f"git add failed: {add.stderr[:300]}", f"scaffold commit failed: {commit.stderr[:300]}" and f"GOAL task creation failed (rc=...): {(r.stderr or r.stdout)[-500:]}". Verified: mocking goals.start to return reason='GOAL task creation failed (rc=1): Traceback /Users/secret/path token=https://u:SECRET@h/r.git' returns 422 with that string verbatim in the body, SECRET included. Apply CREDENTIAL_RE (or a fixed reason set) to r['reason'] before it goes into the JSONResponse, and log the full text instead.

T-0152 item 2 ("bound request bodies before they reach argv") is only half-resolved. request.body() buffers the entire body into memory first; MAX_BODY_BYTES is only checked at line 107, after the fact. Verified: a 40 MB POST to /goals returns 413 but tracemalloc shows a 42.8 MB peak allocation, so the limit bounds nothing an attacker cares about. Check the content-length header before reading, and/or stream via request.stream() aborting once the accumulated length exceeds MAX_BODY_BYTES. The goal-length bound (MAX_GOAL_CHARS) is correctly enforced and is not affected.

tomllib.loads is unguarded, so a malformed .orchestrator/repos.toml raises TOMLDecodeError out of every authenticated goal route as an unhandled 500. Verified: with repos.toml containing '[demo\npath = broken', GET /goals returns 500 while /healthz still returns 200, so the health probe reports the service up while every real route is broken. _resolve_repo already takes care to turn a configured-but-incomplete entry into a clean 404 rather than a 500; a parse failure deserves the same (503 + logged reason). Same class of problem in list_all_goals (line 176): an unreadable or corrupt goals.json in one configured repo fails the whole unfiltered fan-out instead of that one slug.

Cancel is not idempotent against a planner that exits mid-request. goals.stop does `if identity(record): os.killpg(...)` with no guard, so when the planner exits between the liveness check and the signal, ProcessLookupError propagates uncaught through cancel_goal. Verified: patching goals.stop to raise ProcessLookupError makes POST /goals/demo/T-1/cancel return 500 rather than the 200 'stopped' the caller should see for an already-dead goal. kgpt will retry-loop on that. Catch ProcessLookupError/PermissionError around the killpg (or here) and still report stopped.
